input.strategy_title: Graduate Llama Stack to General Availability
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

Llama Stack shipped as Tech Preview and adoption is strong, but enterprise
customers will not build production GenAI applications on a TP component.
Graduating to GA requires API stability commitments, a production support
posture, and closing the quality gaps that TP status currently excuses. The
full inventory of those gaps is not yet known — TP feedback is scattered across
support tickets, and no systematic GA-readiness assessment has been done.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | A GA-readiness assessment inventories the gaps between current TP quality and GA bar (API stability, upgrade paths, scale limits, error handling), producing the definitive GA scope. |
| HLR-2 | P0 | Published API surface carries a stability guarantee: versioned APIs, deprecation policy, and a tested upgrade path from the last two TP releases. |
| HLR-3 | P0 | Production support posture is in place: documented SLO targets, backport policy, and supported configuration matrix. |
| HLR-4 | P1 | Safety guardrails via TrustyAI are a supported, documented integration (not an experimental flag) for GA distributions. |
| HLR-5 | P1 | The Dashboard enables Llama Stack management by default for entitled clusters (no TP opt-in gate). |
| HLR-6 | P2 | Documentation is uplifted to GA standards, including migration notes from TP. |

## Affected Components

- Llama Stack
- TrustyAI
- Dashboard

## Out of Scope

- New Llama Stack feature development beyond GA-bar quality work
- Deprecating alternative GenAI serving paths

## Open Questions

1. The GA scope itself depends on HLR-1's assessment — until it lands, the
   size of the stability and hardening work is an estimate.

# Llama Stack GA-Readiness Assessment

## Description

This Investigation epic resolves the strategy's central unknown: the full
inventory of gaps between Llama Stack's current Tech Preview quality and the
GA bar. Tech Preview feedback is scattered across support tickets and no
systematic GA-readiness assessment has been done. This epic performs that
assessment across the GA-bar dimensions — API stability, upgrade paths, scale
limits, and error handling — and produces the definitive GA scope that all
downstream GA work (API stability guarantee, production support posture, and
guardrails-integration hardening) is sized and confirmed against.

## Scope

- Consolidate Tech Preview feedback from support tickets and known issues
  into a single gap record.
- Assess each GA-bar dimension against the current Llama Stack distribution:
  - API stability of the published surface
  - Upgrade paths from prior Tech Preview releases
  - Scale limits
  - Error handling
- For each gap found, record current state, GA bar, severity, and a
  remediation estimate.
- Assess the TrustyAI guardrails integration against the GA bar and record
  any hardening needed beyond removing its experimental status.
- Publish the definitive GA scope document enumerating the work items
  required for GA graduation, for stakeholder acceptance.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A gap inventory exists covering all four GA-bar dimensions (API stability,
  upgrade paths, scale limits, error handling), each gap recorded with
  current state, GA bar, severity, and remediation estimate.
- Tech Preview feedback from support tickets is consolidated and reflected in
  the inventory.
- The guardrails-integration assessment outcome is recorded (additional
  hardening needed, or none beyond the supported-integration promotion).
- The definitive GA scope document is published and accepted by stakeholders,
  and each downstream GA work stream (API stability, support posture,
  guardrails integration) has its scope confirmed or adjusted against it.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-1 (P0)**: fully covered — this epic is the GA-readiness assessment
  that inventories the gaps between current TP quality and the GA bar and
  produces the definitive GA scope.

# Llama Stack API Stability Guarantee

## Description

This epic delivers the published API stability guarantee that GA requires for
Llama Stack: the published API surface becomes versioned, carries a
deprecation policy, and has a tested upgrade path from the last two Tech
Preview releases. The scope of stability remediation is confirmed against the
GA-readiness assessment's definitive GA scope.

## Scope

- Version the published API surface of the Llama Stack distribution (the
  LlamaStackDistribution-facing API and the OpenAI-compatible REST surface
  the distribution exposes).
- Define and publish a deprecation policy for the published APIs.
- Implement and verify an upgrade path from each of the last two Tech Preview
  releases.
- Remediate the API-stability gaps the GA-readiness assessment assigns to
  this work stream (per its gap inventory), within this epic's scope.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The published API surface is versioned, and the versioning is visible to
  consumers of the distribution.
- A deprecation policy for the published APIs is documented and published.
- Upgrade from each of the last two Tech Preview releases is exercised by an
  automated or repeatable test and passes.
- API-stability gaps allocated to this work stream by the GA-readiness
  assessment are remediated and verified.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-2 (P0)**: fully covered — versioned APIs, deprecation policy, and a
  tested upgrade path from the last two TP releases.

# Llama Stack Production Support Posture

## Description

This epic establishes the production support posture required for Llama Stack
GA: documented SLO targets, a backport policy, and a published supported
configuration matrix. The configuration matrix is grounded in the scale-limit
and error-handling findings of the GA-readiness assessment.

## Scope

- Define and document SLO targets for the production support of Llama Stack.
- Define and publish the backport policy (which releases receive fixes, for
  how long).
- Define the supported configuration matrix and validate the configurations
  it declares supported, incorporating the scale limits established by the
  GA-readiness assessment.
- Record the support posture in the support-process artifacts the platform
  uses for GA components.

## Acceptance Criteria

- SLO targets are documented and published for Llama Stack production
  support.
- The backport policy is documented and published.
- The supported configuration matrix is published, and each configuration it
  declares supported is validated as supported by this epic's work.
- Scale limits from the GA-readiness assessment are reflected in the
  supported configuration matrix.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-3 (P0)**: fully covered — documented SLO targets, backport policy,
  and supported configuration matrix.

# TrustyAI Guardrails as Supported Llama Stack Integration

## Description

This epic promotes safety guardrails via TrustyAI from an experimental flag
to a supported, documented integration for GA Llama Stack distributions. The
TrustyAI side of the integration is brought to a supportable state and
verified against a GA distribution configuration; any guardrails hardening
identified by the GA-readiness assessment is remediated here.

## Scope

- Make the TrustyAI guardrails integration usable with Llama Stack
  distributions without an experimental opt-in flag, as a supported
  configuration of TrustyAI.
- Verify the guardrails integration end to end against a GA-track Llama Stack
  distribution configuration.
- Document the integration for users (setup and usage of guardrails with a
  Llama Stack distribution) — this documentation is part of making the
  integration supported, not the broader GA docs uplift.
- Remediate guardrails-integration gaps recorded by the GA-readiness
  assessment, if any were found beyond the experimental-status gap.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Guardrails via TrustyAI are usable on a Llama Stack distribution with
  supported configuration only — no experimental opt-in flag required.
- The integration is verified working end to end against a GA-track Llama
  Stack distribution configuration.
- User-facing documentation for the guardrails integration exists and
  reflects the supported (non-experimental) configuration.
- Any guardrails gaps recorded by the GA-readiness assessment are remediated
  and verified, or the assessment's record of "no additional gaps" is
  confirmed.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-4 (P1)**: fully covered — TrustyAI guardrails as a supported,
  documented integration (not an experimental flag) for GA distributions.

# Dashboard Llama Stack Management Enabled by Default

## Description

This epic makes Llama Stack management available in the Dashboard by default
for entitled clusters, removing the Tech Preview opt-in gate. Today the
Llama Stack management surfaces sit behind an explicit opt-in; for GA they
must appear automatically wherever the cluster is entitled.

## Scope

- Change the Dashboard's default configuration so that Llama Stack management
  surfaces (navigation, resource views, and management flows) are enabled
  without any opt-in on entitled clusters.
- Gate availability on cluster entitlement, so non-entitled clusters do not
  see Llama Stack management.
- Remove the Tech Preview opt-in gate from the Dashboard configuration
  surface.
- Update any captions, screenshots, or references in the Dashboard that fall
  out of this change (incidental touch-ups, no new content authored).

## Acceptance Criteria

- On an entitled cluster with default Dashboard configuration, Llama Stack
  management is available with no opt-in action by the user or administrator.
- On a cluster without entitlement, Llama Stack management is not surfaced.
- No Tech Preview opt-in gate for Llama Stack management remains in the
  Dashboard configuration.
- The default-enablement behavior is covered by automated tests.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-5 (P1)**: fully covered — the Dashboard enables Llama Stack
  management by default for entitled clusters, with no TP opt-in gate.

# Llama Stack GA Documentation Uplift

## Description

This epic uplifts Llama Stack documentation to GA standards, including
migration notes from Tech Preview. It runs last: the documentation describes
what was actually built — the published API stability guarantee, the
production support posture, the supported TrustyAI guardrails integration,
and default Dashboard availability.

## Scope

Content outline (authored inside this epic):

- GA-standard Llama Stack documentation: installation, configuration, and
  supported-usage guidance at GA quality, referencing the published supported
  configuration matrix.
- API stability documentation: the versioned API surface and the deprecation
  policy as published.
- Migration notes from Tech Preview: how to move from the last two TP
  releases along the tested upgrade path, including any breaking changes and
  their remedies.
- Guardrails integration documentation pointing at the supported TrustyAI
  integration.
- Dashboard availability notes reflecting default enablement on entitled
  clusters.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Llama Stack documentation meets GA documentation standards as defined by
  the Red Hat docs content process.
- Migration notes from Tech Preview exist and cover the tested upgrade path
  from the last two TP releases.
- The documentation is technically reviewed against the implemented behavior
  of the GA deliverables (API stability, support posture, guardrails
  integration, Dashboard availability) and discrepancies found in review are
  fixed.
- Documentation claims that reference the supported configuration matrix,
  SLO targets, and backport policy match the published support posture.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-6 (P2)**: fully covered — documentation uplifted to GA standards,
  including migration notes from Tech Preview.
